h: Tips for a splash of Bristol
p: Most visitors spend a couple of hours at the aquarium, which leaves plenty of time to explore the rest of the Harbourside. Because standard tickets let you go round more than once on the day you visit, you can pop out for lunch and come back if the little ones want another look at their favourite tanks.

Plan around the feeding times and talks if you can. Hearing the keepers explain what the animals eat and how they're looked after adds a lot to the visit, and kids love watching the action. Ask at the entrance what's on that day.

Getting there: with no dedicated car park, it's worth thinking about public transport or one of the nearby city car parks. Bristol Temple Meads station is a reasonable walk or a short bus ride away, and the harbour ferries are a lovely, fun way to arrive by water if they're running.

The Harbourside is full of other things to see. The SS Great Britain, Brunel's pioneering steamship, sits in its dry dock across the water and is a brilliant day out in its own right. M Shed, the free city museum on Prince's Wharf, tells Bristol's story from its trading past to the present day, while the cranes outside are a reminder of the docks' working history.

For food, there's no shortage of choice around the waterfront, from casual cafés to street food. If the sun comes out, grab an ice cream and watch the boats on the harbour. It's a lovely way to round off a day in the city.
